content:
iPhone Bumper cases have been beloved by fans since the iPhone 4, but in recent years, choices on the market have dwindled. For those seeking a minimalist protective case, Rhinoshield offers a noteworthy option.

Apple re-entered the bumper case market last year with the iPhone Air. I had hoped Apple would extend its bumper case to the iPhone 18 Pro (just as it expanded the Clear Case to the iPhone 11), but unfortunately that never came to fruition. While searching for alternatives, I came across Rhinoshield's Minimalist Impact Bumper case.

Key Details

The fit of the Impact Bumper is similar to most bumper cases — there's very minimal lip around the screen and slightly more around the back. One unique design feature I really appreciate is the special support structure that keeps the camera plateau and lenses from making direct contact with whatever surface you set the phone on. This is particularly important for the aluminum 17 Pro and 18 Pro. This design makes the case far more protective than the average bumper case, while also solving that annoying wobble issue when using the phone on a flat surface.

That said, the fit isn't ideal. It's a bit loose — the edges flex outward fairly easily — and I'm a little concerned they might stretch out over time. Even so, I don't think the phone is likely to fly out if dropped (I accidentally tested this once). That said, the entire case is made of hard plastic rather than rubber, so hopefully it holds up over the long term. Rhinoshield says the case is made from a single material, making it 100% recyclable.

The case is available in three colors matched to the iPhone 18 Pro: White, Blue, and Black (sorry, fans of the wine red). I have the blue version, which is close to but not quite the same shade as Glacier.

The Downsides

There are definitely some drawbacks, though. My main complaint is that the buttons are really hard to press. For some reason they made them nearly flush with the case, and the tactile feedback is pretty mushy.

The overall material choice may also be a downside. To me, it feels cheaper than Apple's iPhone Air bumper case, though some people might actually prefer this feel. Personally, I prefer it over the typical TPU/rubber clear case material. However, the material combined with the looser design seems to attract lint from your pocket fairly easily.

If you use Apple's Wrist Strap or Crossbody Strap, note that this case doesn't have the necessary attachment points.

Conclusion

The Rhinoshield bumper case is far from perfect, and I'm still hoping Apple will extend its bumper case to other iPhone models. In the end, though, I decided to keep it for one simple reason: it lets me enjoy a near-bare-phone feel without worrying about the fragile aluminum frame getting dented or chipped. As far as I know, this bumper is typically only sold on Rhinoshield's official website, priced at around $30, which with shipping ends up matching Apple's $39 price point. You can purchase the Rhinoshield Minimalist Impact Bumper here. (Amazon occasionally has a listing, so you might try there as well.)
